title: Immersions of algebraic spaces: affine tests and Zariski locality
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and use algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] and sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. An immersion means a representable morphism whose every scheme base change is a closed immersion followed by an open immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion]. For any $f:X\to Y$, the following are equivalent: $f$ is an immersion; every affine scheme $V\to Y$ has $X\times_YV$ represented by a scheme and $X\times_YV\to V$ is an immersion; there is a covering of $Y$ by open subspaces $Y_a$ such that each $X\times_YY_a\to Y_a$ is an immersion. Immersions are preserved by arbitrary algebraic-space base change. No representability of $f$ is assumed before testing these conditions.

source.place: Tag 03M4 (lemma-closed-immersion-local), immersion case (1), (3), (5); base change: spaces.tex Tag 02YW (lemma-base-change-immersions).

proof.text: First prove arbitrary base-change stability directly from the scheme-test definition, without invoking an immersion-locality criterion. If $f:X\to Y$ is an immersion and $Y'\to Y$ is any algebraic-space map, the fibre product $X'=X\times_YY'$ exists as an algebraic space. For every scheme $T\to Y'$, the universal property gives $X'\times_{Y'}T\simeq X\times_YT$, over $T$. The right side is a scheme and its projection to $T$ is an immersion by the definition of $f$. Thus $X'\to Y'$ is representable and is an immersion. This also proves the affine-test condition from the immersion condition. Restricting to any Zariski open cover proves the forward locality implication (and the one-member cover $Y$ proves existence of such a cover).

source.place: Tag 03M4 (lemma-closed-immersion-local), (1) implies (2) implies (3) and (1) implies (5); spaces.tex Tag 02YW (lemma-base-change-immersions), scheme-test argument.

proof.text: Assume the affine-test condition and fix an arbitrary scheme $T\to Y$. Put $E=X\times_YT$, an algebraic space, and take a small affine open cover $T=\bigcup_iT_i$, available from the definition of a scheme. Put $E_i=E\times_TT_i$. The hypothesis applied to $T_i\to Y$ says that $E_i$ is represented by a scheme and $E_i\to T_i$ is an immersion. The functor $E$ is an fppf sheaf; since Zariski coverings are fppf coverings, it is a Zariski sheaf. Each $E_i\to E$ is a subfunctor inclusion representable by open immersions: for a scheme $W\to E$ its pullback is $W\times_TT_i\to W$, a base change of the open immersion $T_i\to T$. For any such $W$, the inverse images of the opens $T_i$ cover $W$, and the restricted sections lie in $E_i$ by the fibre-product universal property. These are exactly the representability, open-inclusion and covering hypotheses of the scheme representability criterion. Apply it to the functor $E$ on $S$-schemes to conclude that $E$ is a scheme. Its values and the affine cover are small in the fixed size convention. This recovers representability without assuming it for $f$.

source.place: Tag 03M4, affine tests imply scheme tests; direct Zariski gluing via schemes.tex Tag 01JJ (lemma-glue-functors), in place of the stronger etale-atlas intermediate condition.

proof.text: For the scheme morphism $E\to T$ just constructed, each restriction over $T_i$ is the immersion $E_i\to T_i$. Apply the scheme near-image locality lemma: the opens $T_i$ cover $T$, so they cover the image of $E\to T$ as required. It follows that $E\to T$ is an immersion. Since $T\to Y$ was arbitrary, all scheme tests are immersions and $f$ is an immersion by its definition. This proves the reverse affine-test implication.

source.place: Tag 03M4, (3) implies (1), using schemes.tex Tag 01JJ and morphisms.tex Tag 0FCZ (lemma-check-immersion).

proof.text: Finally suppose a Zariski open cover $(Y_a\subseteq Y)_a$ has immersion restrictions $X_a=X\times_YY_a\to Y_a$. Fix any scheme $T\to Y$ and put $E=X\times_YT$. By the meaning of an open subspace and a Zariski covering, $T_a=T\times_YY_a$ are open subschemes covering $T$. The sheaf $E_a=E\times_TT_a\simeq X_a\times_{Y_a}T_a$ is a scheme, and $E_a\to T_a$ is an immersion by the assumed scheme-test property of $X_a\to Y_a$. Each $E_a\to E$ is representable by open immersions: its pullback by $W\to E$ is the inverse-image open $W\times_TT_a\subseteq W$. These opens cover every test $W$ because the $T_a$ cover $T$. Also $E$ is an fppf, hence Zariski, sheaf. The scheme representability criterion therefore applies to $(E_a\subseteq E)_a$ and gives a scheme representing $E$. Now apply near-image locality to $E\to T$ and the open cover $(T_a)_a$ to conclude that $E\to T$ is an immersion. All scheme tests have been verified, so $f$ is an immersion. Empty covers cause no exception: then the target test scheme is empty; the empty family in the representability criterion gives the empty scheme, and near-image locality explicitly permits the empty index set. No quasi-compactness, separatedness of $Y$, or finiteness of either cover was used.

source.place: Tag 03M4, (5) implies (1), expanded by schemes.tex Tag 01JJ and morphisms.tex Tag 0FCZ; spaces.tex Tag 02YU (definition-immersion) for open subspaces.

proof_origin.place: Tag 03M4 (lemma-closed-immersion-local), restricted to (1),(3),(5); direct Zariski representability argument using 01JJ and 0FCZ. Base-change argument is the definition underlying spaces.tex Tag 02YW.
